results.note: Single most valuable investment: make the backend the single source of truth for the frontend contract and prove it end-to-end. Today GREEN CI can ship a backend field rename/type change because (a) the OpenAPI contract fingerprint in tests/test_api_contracts.py deliberately collapses every response to just {$ref|type|title} and never descends into the referenced schema's fields, and (b) frontend/src/types/*.ts are hand-written with no codegen from the schema. The one high-leverage guard that dissolves the whole frontend/backend schema-drift class: add a committed schema artifact generated from app.openapi() (or per-model model_json_schema()), generate the TS types from it, and add ONE CI job that regenerates both and fails on any diff (git diff --exit-code). That job replaces the brittle hand-maintained fingerprint snapshot, the ALLOWED_TYPES mirror test, and the hand-curated ui_contracts fixtures with a mechanical, exhaustive, field-level invariant. The second-highest guard is a clean-subprocess execution lane for a deployed pipeline .py (only the installed wheel's deps on PATH) to actually honor the standalone-portability promise that test_e2e.py only round-trips in-process.

findings.title: OpenAPI contract fingerprint is field-blind: backend schema field renames/type changes ship GREEN
findings.location: tests/test_api_contracts.py:8 (_normalise_schema), :21 (_api_contract_fingerprint), :512 (test_openapi_contract_fingerprint_matches_expected_snapshot)
findings.description: _normalise_schema() collapses every response/request to only {"$ref": ...} or {type,title}; it never follows the $ref into components/schemas, so the fingerprint is identical whether TrainResponse.glm_relativities is renamed, retyped (float->str), made optional, or dropped. The snapshot test therefore proves only that the path->ref WIRING is stable, not that any field/type the frontend consumes is stable. Combined with the fact that frontend/src/types/*.ts (node.ts, trace.ts, banding.ts, guards.ts) are hand-authored with NO generation from the schema, a backend field-level change is invisible to the entire CI. The only field-level protections are (a) the single ALLOWED_TYPES list comparison in test_frontend_backend_contract.py and (b) ~45 hand-maintained JSON fixtures in tests/fixtures/ui_contracts validated against Pydantic models in test_backend_frontend_contracts.py — both of which a developer must remember to update, so they do not detect drift, they only assert hand-written parity.
findings.recommended_guard: Make the backend schema the single source of truth and enforce mechanically: (1) a committed artifact (e.g. frontend/src/types/api.generated.ts) produced by exporting app.openapi() / model_json_schema() and running an OpenAPI->TS generator; (2) a CI job 'schema-sync' that regenerates the artifact and the OpenAPI JSON, then runs `git diff --exit-code` so any backend schema change that is not reflected in committed generated types fails the build; (3) delete the hand-maintained fingerprint snapshot and ALLOWED_TYPES mirror in favour of the generated diff. This dissolves the entire frontend/backend schema-drift class at field granularity.
findings.prevents: frontend/backend schema drift (field rename, type change, required/optional flip, dropped field) — the class the current fingerprint + ALLOWED_TYPES + fixtures only partially and manually cover.

findings.title: Standalone-.py portability promise is never exercised in a clean interpreter for DEPLOYED/codegen output
findings.location: tests/test_e2e.py:1 (parse->execute->codegen->re-parse all in-process); tests/test_starter_pipeline_e2e.py:519 (only the `init` scaffold runs in subprocess); .github/workflows/ci.yml:85-110 (package-smoke installs wheel but only runs package_smoke_check.py + `haute --help`)
findings.description: The portability promise ('the emitted .py runs standalone') is asserted in test_e2e.py only as an IN-PROCESS round-trip: graph_to_code() then parse_pipeline_source() in the same interpreter that already has polars/catboost/rustystats and the full repo on sys.path. The only true clean-subprocess execution is the `haute init` starter scaffold (test_starter_pipeline_e2e.py:519 shells out with sys.executable). The package-smoke CI lane installs the wheel into a fresh venv but only imports haute, checks static assets/routes, and runs `haute --help` — it never executes a real generated/deployed pipeline .py end-to-end against ONLY the wheel's runtime deps. So an emitted file that imports a dev-only or test-only symbol, relies on repo-relative paths, or depends on a transitive dep not in [project.dependencies] would still pass every gate.
findings.recommended_guard: Add a CI lane (extend package-smoke) that, inside the wheel-only venv: scaffolds or loads a representative pipeline, calls the deploy/codegen path to emit the standalone .py, then runs `./.pkg-wheel/bin/python <emitted>.py` (or `python -m pytest` on a generated test) in that clean process and asserts the printed premium matches a golden value. This proves the emitted artifact runs with only [project.dependencies] installed.
findings.prevents: standalone-.py portability regressions (missing/incorrect import in codegen output, reliance on dev-group deps, repo-relative path leakage) that in-process round-trip tests structurally cannot catch.

findings.title: No validate-vs-serve numeric parity gate for the deployed/containerized scorer
findings.location: tests/test_deploy_expected_output_validation.py (validate path only); tests/test_deploy_contract_integrity.py:1 (feature-contract + test-quote failure handling); tests/test_deploy_container.py (container build, no numeric parity grep hit)
findings.description: validate_deploy()/score_test_quotes() and the feature-contract guard are well tested, and the container build is tested, but no test asserts that the SERVED/containerized scorer returns byte-identical (or within-tolerance) numbers to the in-editor execute_graph()/validate path for the same quote. The 'deploy validate passed but serve returns different numbers' class (feature-order skew, missing artifact substitution at serve time, contract drift between bundle and runtime) is exactly the seam between the two code paths and is the one not pinned.
findings.recommended_guard: Add a parity test: take a golden quote, compute the premium via the in-editor execute path AND via the deployed scorer entrypoint (the same callable the container/serve route invokes), assert equality within the documented tolerance. Run it in the wheel-only venv lane so it doubles as deploy-portability coverage.
findings.prevents: deploy validate-vs-serve divergence (the served artifact silently producing different numbers than validation approved).

findings.title: Coverage gates measure line/branch reachability, not behaviour; mutation (the behavioural gate) is path-filtered and not required on main
findings.location: .github/workflows/mutation.yml:6-12 (PR trigger filtered to src/haute/**/*.py, tests/**, mutation/**); scripts/run_mutation_suite.py:304 (_select_targets_for_changed_files skips when no mutation-relevant file changed); pyproject.toml:158 fail_under=90 + [tool.haute.critical_coverage]
findings.description: The 90% global + per-file critical coverage gates prove lines/branches are EXECUTED, not that an assertion would fail if the behaviour changed — a test can import-and-touch a critical module (parser.py, executor.py, _model_scorer.py) for coverage credit without asserting correctness. Mutation testing is the only behavioural gate, but: (1) it runs only on PRs whose diff touches src/haute/**/*.py or tests/** (a change to e.g. pyproject thresholds, a config JSON, or codegen template data files that affects behaviour but not those globs runs zero mutants); (2) on a direct push to main mutation.yml's pull_request trigger does not fire, so a force-merge or admin push lands with no mutation check; (3) mutation is a separate workflow, so unless branch protection lists it as required, a PR can merge while it is queued/failing.
findings.recommended_guard: (a) Add a small always-on mutation smoke (a handful of highest-value mutants on parser.py/executor.py/_model_scorer.py) to the blocking CI 'backend' lane so every change pays a behavioural check; (b) document/enforce that mutation.yml is a REQUIRED status check in branch protection; (c) broaden the mutation path filter to include codegen template/data and config files that influence pricing behaviour.
findings.prevents: coverage-gaming silent wrongness (lines covered, behaviour unverified) and parse->codegen->execute equivalence regressions slipping past line-coverage when the diff dodges the mutation path filter.

findings.title: Perf and mutation lanes do not gate pushes to main; perf has no committed baseline so it only catches absolute-budget blowups, not regressions
findings.location: .github/workflows/performance.yml:4-6 (workflow_dispatch + weekly cron only); .github/workflows/ci.yml:35-54 (PR perf lane runs run_perf_suite but gates only on absolute budgets); scripts/run_perf_suite.py:59 (_budget_violations compares against fixed max_total/max_test seconds, no baseline delta)
findings.description: The standalone performance.yml workflow is cron/dispatch only — it never runs on PRs or main pushes, so it cannot block a merge. The PR-time perf lane in ci.yml IS blocking but run_perf_suite only fails on absolute budget violations (max-total/max-test seconds) and on skipped/xfailed perf tests; there is no committed performance baseline and no per-test regression-vs-baseline delta. A change that doubles a hot path's time but stays under the 120s per-test ceiling ships GREEN. Artifacts are uploaded but nothing consumes the previous run to compute a delta.
findings.recommended_guard: Commit a perf baseline (per-test medians) and make the PR perf lane fail when a test regresses beyond a tolerance vs baseline (ratchet), not only when it exceeds an absolute ceiling; regenerate the baseline deliberately like the test-debt budget. Optionally run the perf lane on main pushes too so the baseline tracks merged state.
findings.prevents: silent performance regressions within the absolute budget; perf coverage being merged without ever running (cron-only workflow).

findings.title: Cache-integrity invariants are unit-tested but there is no cross-process / concurrent-writer durability lane
findings.location: tests/test_json_cache_integrity.py:1-16 (single-process, in-test concurrency via threads at :259); .github/workflows/ci.yml (no dedicated cache-integrity / concurrency lane; backend runs the suite under -n workers with --timeout-method=signal on POSIX)
findings.description: Cache integrity (schema-fingerprint vs content-hash arbitration, atomic temp-dir promotion, stale-mirror prevention) is covered by strong single-process tests using in-process threads. But the real failure mode is multi-PROCESS: two `haute` invocations or a serve worker + a CLI rebuild racing on the same .cache directory, and crash-during-promote durability. Thread-based tests share a GIL and an interpreter and cannot reproduce OS-level rename/lock races or a killed process mid-write. There is also no Windows leg for the cache-integrity suite specifically (platform-smoke runs path/debt/file_ops tests, not test_json_cache_integrity.py), yet the atomic-write reader-contention debt entries in test_test_debt.py (08c3e550, 716bebf0) show Windows rename semantics differ.
findings.recommended_guard: Add a cross-process cache durability test (spawn 2+ subprocesses contending on one cache dir; kill one mid-promote; assert the survivor reads a consistent, non-stale parquet and the killed write leaves no half-promoted layer) and include test_json_cache_integrity.py + the new cross-process test in the windows-latest platform-smoke matrix so rename/lock divergence is gated on the OS that actually differs.
findings.prevents: cache-integrity corruption under concurrent processes / crash-during-write, and Windows-specific cache races, which the current GIL-bound thread tests cannot exercise.

findings.title: mkdocs --strict (docstring/cross-reference breakage) only runs on docs/** path pushes, not on PRs that edit rendered docstrings
findings.location: .github/workflows/docs.yml:3-8 (push to main filtered to docs/** and mkdocs.yml; no pull_request trigger)
findings.description: docs.yml builds with --strict (which fails on broken mkdocstrings references) but only triggers on push to main when docs/** or mkdocs.yml changed. mkdocstrings renders Python docstrings from src/haute/**, so a PR that breaks a cross-reference or an autodoc target in a module docstring will NOT trigger docs.yml (the path filter excludes src/**), and the main backend CI never runs mkdocs. The broken docs build is only discovered after merge, on the main push — and only if that same push happened to touch docs/**.
findings.recommended_guard: Add a pull_request trigger to docs.yml (build-only, no deploy) OR add `uv run mkdocs build --strict` to the blocking backend preflight, so docstring/reference breakage in src/** is caught pre-merge.
findings.prevents: post-merge docs build breakage from src/** docstring/reference changes that the docs path filter currently lets through.

findings.title: Backend CI matrix tests 3 Python versions only on Linux; package-smoke, deploy, and contract lanes are single-version single-OS
findings.location: .github/workflows/ci.yml:16-18 (matrix 3.11/3.12/3.13 ubuntu only), :85-110 (package-smoke 3.12 ubuntu only), :112-128 (platform-smoke runs only a 4-file path/debt subset on win/mac)
findings.description: The full backend suite + coverage gates run across 3.11/3.12/3.13 but only on ubuntu-latest. platform-smoke on windows/macos runs ONLY tests/test_path_resolution.py, test_pipeline_runtime_path_validation.py, test_test_debt.py, test_file_ops.py — so the parser/executor/codegen/scorer/deploy/cache behaviour is never executed on Windows or macOS in CI, despite the codebase carrying explicit Windows-specific branches (npm.cmd resolution in hatch_build.py:117-124 and cli helpers, MoveFileExW rename semantics, drive-letter pyvenv guards in both preflight scripts). package-smoke (wheel/sdist install + standalone) runs only on 3.12/ubuntu, so a wheel that fails to install or run on Windows or on 3.11/3.13 ships green.
findings.recommended_guard: Run package-smoke (or at least a wheel install + emitted-.py execution smoke) on the windows/macos matrix, and broaden platform-smoke to include a small parser/executor/codegen/cache behavioural slice on Windows. Lowest-effort high-value: add windows-latest to package-smoke.
findings.prevents: OS-specific and Python-version-specific install/runtime breakage (path, rename, npm-resolution, drive-letter) that the Linux-3.12-only smoke lanes miss.

results.note: The single highest-value prevention investment is a PARSE -> CODEGEN -> EXECUTE differential harness (Guard #1). It is the only guard that dissolves the system's #1-ranked risk class (codegen/executor semantic non-equivalence, cluster C1) at the level where it actually bites: VALUES, not structure. The existing capstone roundtrip property test (tests/test_codegen_roundtrip_property.py) is deliberately scoped to source-byte + structural equivalence and explicitly budgets out execution; tests/test_pipeline.py runs p.run()/p.score() on the in-memory DSL/executor object, never on a codegen-emitted-then-reparsed standalone file. So the confirmed `return <first>` passthrough bodies (_make_passthrough_builder for optimiser/optimiserApply/modelling/scenarioExpander) and the liveSwitch hard-wired 'live' branch pass every current gate while silently no-op'ing or mis-routing when the SAVED file runs standalone -- the README's 'it's just Python, take it with you' promise. One harness (codegen(g) -> write -> run via pipeline.run()/score() under source in {live,batch} -> assert frame-equal to execute_graph(g)), parametrized over `frozenset(NodeType)` minus submodels, turns 3+ confirmed divergences plus every future passthrough/wiring regression into a red test, and pairs naturally with a registry invariant (Guard #2) asserting every stateful NodeType routes through one shared apply_*_from_config helper so the divergence becomes impossible to express. These two are strictly higher leverage than the dozens of per-finding gate tweaks.

findings.title: No execution-level parse->codegen->execute differential harness: structural roundtrip passes while standalone VALUES diverge
findings.location: tests/test_codegen_roundtrip_property.py (structural-only); tests/test_pipeline.py (executor-only); src/haute/_codegen_builders.py:784-858 (_make_passthrough_builder + liveSwitch _gen_live_switch:522)
findings.description: The capstone roundtrip property test asserts ONLY (a) parse(codegen(g)) preserves representable semantics and (b) codegen(parse(codegen(g))) is byte-identical source. Its own docstring budgets execution out. Separately, test_pipeline.py exercises p.run()/p.score() but on the in-memory Pipeline object built from the DSL -- i.e. it runs the EXECUTOR path, never a codegen-emitted file reparsed and executed standalone. The result: _make_passthrough_builder emits `return {first}` for OPTIMISER, OPTIMISER_APPLY, MODELLING, SCENARIO_EXPANDER (confirmed at _codegen_builders.py:847-858), and _gen_live_switch hard-routes the 'live' input, so the generated standalone file performs a no-op / wrong-branch where the executor applies real logic. Every current gate is green; the saved pipeline mis-prices when run outside the canvas. This is the architecture's #1-ranked risk (semantic equivalence, heat-map score 10) and is currently unguarded at the value level.
findings.recommended_guard: Add tests/test_codegen_execute_differential.py: for a corpus graph covering frozenset(NodeType) - {SUBMODEL, SUBMODEL_PORT} (reuse the capstone _capstone_root_graph fixture), do graph_to_code_multi(g) -> write to tmp -> write sidecars -> load the standalone module and call pipeline.run() (source=batch) and pipeline.score(df) (source=live) -> assert_frame_equal against execute_graph(g) for each output node, for BOTH source values. Drive it with deterministic tiny artifacts (a real saved optimiser JSON, a tiny .cbm/.rsglm or stubbed score_from_config) so optimiserApply/liveSwitch/modelScore/scenarioExpander are exercised, not skipped. Make it a required CI step in scripts/preflight.sh backend lane.
findings.prevents: Cluster C1 entirely: 'Generated liveSwitch body hard-wires live input', 'Generated optimiserApply body is a pure passthrough', 'Passthrough-body node types (optimiser/modelling/scenarioExpander/optimiserApply) no-op under standalone pipeline.run()'. Also any future codegen template that drifts from its executor builder (edge-join base/join role swap, constant/dataSource literal-vs-config drift).

findings.title: No registry invariant that every stateful NodeType shares one apply_*_from_config helper between codegen and executor
findings.location: src/haute/_registry.py (NODE_REGISTRY has exec+codegen+column_contract but no shared-runtime-helper slot); src/haute/_codegen_builders.py:784 (_make_passthrough_builder bypasses any shared helper)
findings.description: The architecture states the pricing math has ONE implementation: both _builders.py and _codegen_builders.py call apply_banding_from_config / apply_rating_step_from_config / score_from_config / execute_edge_join. But the passthrough node types (optimiser/optimiserApply/modelling/scenarioExpander) and liveSwitch are the exact set that DO NOT share a config-driven runtime helper -- codegen emits an inert body, the executor builder does the work. The registry already enforces 'exactly one exec AND one codegen builder per NodeType' (validate_registry_complete) and the codebase already uses the `set(declarations) == set(NodeType)` idiom in 4 places (test_chunk_plan, test_projection_planner, test_codegen_split, column contracts). The missing structural rule is: every NodeType that transforms data must route BOTH sides through a single shared apply_<type>_from_config(first, config, base_dir) entry point, so a no-op generated body becomes impossible to write.
findings.recommended_guard: (1) Refactor each passthrough NodeType to a shared apply_*_from_config helper in graph_utils (apply_optimiser_apply_from_config, select_live_switch_input(source, **frames), etc.) called by both the exec builder and the codegen-emitted body. (2) Add a registry invariant test: for every NodeType not on an explicit STATELESS_PASSTHROUGH allowlist, assert NODE_REGISTRY[nt] exposes a shared_runtime_helper and that the codegen template string contains a call to it (or, more robustly, that the Guard #1 differential harness covers it). Failing closed forces a new stateful NodeType to wire the shared helper before it can be registered.
findings.prevents: Cluster C1 at the root (makes the divergence inexpressible, complementing Guard #1 which detects it). Future-proofs every new transform node against the same class.

findings.title: Parser has no structure-conservation invariant; a test actively PINS the silent node-loss bug
findings.location: tests/test_parser.py:836-865 (test_duplicate_function_names_both_appear asserts the buggy collapse); src/haute/_graph_builders.py:73; src/haute/_ast_helpers.py; src/haute/_parser_regex.py; src/haute/_parser_submodels.py
findings.description: Cluster C5 is 7 parser bugs that all share one root cause: structure-loss boundaries silently degrade instead of raising. There is no single invariant asserting that parsing conserves graph structure. Worse, test_parser.py:862 explicitly asserts ids.count('step') == 2 for duplicate function names -- it PINS the silent-collision behaviour ('two GraphNodes share the same id') that the executor then collapses, the opposite of the CLAUDE.md fail-loud mandate. Async-def nodes, posonly/kwonly params (V042), nested submodels (V040), submodel name collisions, regex-fallback dropping all submodels, and implicit cross-boundary edges are each an independent silent drop with no umbrella guard. The project already counts node types elsewhere with set()==set(NodeType); the analogous parser guard is absent.
findings.recommended_guard: Add a structure-conservation property test (Hypothesis over decorator-DSL source corpora): assert that for any parseable @pipeline file, the count of decorated @pipeline.<type> functions == number of non-container GraphNodes, that every distinct top-level function name maps to a distinct node id (else ParseError), and that the union of declared param-name references resolves to existing nodes or raises. Pair with a fail-loud assertion replacing test_duplicate_function_names_both_appear: pytest.raises(ParseError, match='duplicate') so the comparator can no longer hide the loss. Add a regex-fallback-vs-AST node/edge-count parity case so a syntax error in the main file cannot silently null all submodels.
findings.prevents: Cluster C5 (all 7): duplicate-name collapse, async-def invisibility, posonly/kwonly param drop (V042), submodel-name collision, regex-fallback submodel wipe, nested-submodel drop (V040), implicit cross-boundary edge drop, chained/keyword submodel() drop.

findings.title: Frontend NodeType list (nodeTypes.ts / api/types.ts) is never mechanically checked against the backend NodeType enum
findings.location: frontend/src/utils/nodeTypes.ts:5-25 (NODE_TYPES); frontend/src/api/types.ts; src/haute/_types.py (NodeType enum); .github/workflows/ci.yml (backend + frontend are disjoint jobs)
findings.description: The frontend hand-maintains NODE_TYPES (20 string literals) plus per-type defaultConfig/metadata, and api/types.ts mirrors the wire contract; the backend NodeType enum is the source of truth. CI runs backend (preflight.sh --backend-only) and frontend (preflight.sh --frontend-only) as SEPARATE jobs that never share a process, and preflight.sh runs them in disjoint branches. No test asserts that the set of frontend NODE_TYPES values equals {nt.value for nt in NodeType}. A node type added/renamed on either side (e.g. a new transform node, or a value-string change) ships a frontend that can construct a node the backend rejects, or omits a palette entry, with zero CI signal. The architecture explicitly calls this the 'frontend mirrors the wire contract (api/types.ts <-> types/guards.ts) ... its own cache-identity surface that must agree with the backend' obligation -- but nothing enforces the enum half of it.
findings.recommended_guard: Add a schema-PARITY gate: a small backend script emits the authoritative contract (NodeType values, and ideally each node's default config keys / required wire fields) to a JSON snapshot; a frontend vitest (or a Python test that reads nodeTypes.ts via a generated constants file) asserts Object.values(NODE_TYPES) deep-equals the emitted set and that api/types.ts node-type union matches. Wire it into BOTH preflight lanes (or a new cross-language job) so neither side can drift alone. This is the client analogue of validate_registry_complete().
findings.prevents: Cluster C16/C17 drift class and frontend/backend enum desync generally; latent 'node type exists on one side only' bugs that currently have no test. Strengthens the wire-contract guarantee the architecture names as a defining obligation.

findings.title: JSON-shred conservation property exists for inference->shred but not for fingerprint-collision, $value/dotted-key collapse, or freshness identity
findings.location: tests/test_json_shred_properties.py:51-169 (emitted+skipped==visited, inference path only); src/haute/_json_shred.py:108-147 (_v2_fingerprint silent continue), :1199-1221 ($value collision), :1203/1213 (dotted-key path), _data_file_matches (mtime fast-path); src/haute/routes/json_cache.py
findings.description: There IS a strong conservation law for the inference->shred row path (every array element at an emitting depth is emitted-or-counted; emitted+skipped==visited). But the cluster-C2 bugs live at three boundaries that law does NOT cover: (1) _v2_fingerprint silently `continue`s past non-dict tables/columns so two structurally-different on-disk configs collapse to one schema_fingerprint and a stale cache is judged fresh (V015 $value-leaf drop, V016 dotted-key None-collapse are the same family -- a key literally named '$value' or containing '.' silently loses every record/value); (2) _data_file_matches returns fresh on (size, mtime_ns) WITHOUT hashing, so a byte-changing rewrite that preserves both serves stale; (3) the status/validity route reads the config WITHOUT validate_v2_schema. None of these has a collision/loud-loss test.
findings.recommended_guard: Extend the shred property suite with: (a) a fingerprint-INJECTIVITY property -- Hypothesis over pairs of distinct valid+malformed v2 configs asserting distinct configs never share schema_fingerprint (forces _v2_fingerprint to raise on non-dict instead of continue); (b) a no-silent-loss property over adversarial keys including literal '$value' and keys containing '.', asserting either every source value is emitted/skip-accounted or ApiInputSchemaError is raised (kills V015/V016); (c) a freshness-CONSERVATION test: any byte change to the data file (size/mtime held constant) must invalidate the cache -- pinning the sha256 verification. Also call validate_v2_schema inside the status route so the 422 path fires.
findings.prevents: Cluster C2 (all 5) plus V015 ($value collision silent table drop), V016 (dotted-key silent value loss). The named wave-2-cache-integrity concern.

findings.title: Rating-key Python-mirror vs Polars-twin property is strong but explicitly excludes the save-vs-apply dtype divergence and non-integer Float32
findings.location: tests/test_rating_key_agreement.py:259-285 (_expr_canonical compares mirror vs REAL Polars -- excellent); docstring lines 23-27 carve out Float32; C6 finding 2 (save-time banding-source dtype vs apply-time optimiserApply input dtype) untested; src/haute/_rating.py, src/haute/routes/_optimiser_service.py, src/haute/_builders.py
findings.description: This is the model guard the audit wants -- it canonicalises every value through BOTH normalise_rating_key and a real pl.Series/_rating_key_expr round trip, with a dtype grid. But two C6 gaps remain: (1) the docstring states 'non-integer Float32 keys are outside the enrichment-agreement guarantee' (the trace JSON boundary loses Float32 dtype), so the mirror can still silently disagree there; (2) ratebook factor levels are canonicalised at SAVE time against the banding-source column dtype but APPLIED against the optimiserApply input column dtype -- a dtype divergence for the same factor yields a silent neutral-1.0 miss, and no test pins save-dtype != apply-dtype agreement. The property currently proves the twin agrees in-process; it does not prove the SAVED ratebook still matches when applied against a differently-typed column.
findings.recommended_guard: Extend the existing property with a dtype-MATRIX differential: (a) carry the factor column's original dtype through the trace JSON boundary and assert Float32 non-integer cells canonicalise via pl.Series(dtype=Float32).cast(Utf8) equal to the engine (close the Float32 carve-out); (b) add a save->apply round-trip property: build a ratebook by solving against a banding-source column of dtype D1, then apply it against an optimiserApply input column of dtype D2 over {Float32, Float64, Int32, Int64}, asserting either a match or a LOUD save-vs-apply dtype-mismatch error -- never a silent neutral-1.0.
findings.prevents: Cluster C6 (both findings): normalise_rating_key vs _rating_key_expr Float32 disagreement; ratebook save-dtype vs apply-dtype silent neutral-1.0 miss.

findings.title: Fingerprint-COMPLETENESS is asserted ad hoc per cache, not as a single 'every output-affecting input is in the key' invariant
findings.location: src/haute/_cache.py (graph_fingerprint, canonical_json); src/haute/deploy/_schema.py (infer_output_schema keys on graph_fingerprint only); src/haute/_model_scorer.py (id(scoring_model)); _json_shred.py (schema_fingerprint); _cache.py:198-201,429-432 (non-injective node/extra-key joins V035)
findings.description: Clusters C3 + C11 + C12 + parts of C2/C16 share one root: a fingerprint omits an input class that changes the output (model-artifact bytes/version, preamble utility module resolved via sys.path, mtime ns-precision, duplicate-key handling) OR a join is non-injective (V035: node id / extra_key containing '|' or newline collides distinct graphs to one fingerprint; V034: NaN in a set makes canonical_json non-deterministic). These are tested, if at all, one cache at a time. There is no meta-property that, given a function producing a cache key, asserts perturbing ANY output-affecting input perturbs the key, and that the key encoder is injective under adversarial separators.
findings.recommended_guard: (1) Injectivity property for canonical_json / graph_fingerprint: Hypothesis over node ids and extra_keys containing '|', '\n', and set/frozenset with NaN, asserting distinct logical inputs never collide and identical logical inputs always agree (kills V034, V035). (2) A 'fingerprint completeness' table-test: enumerate (cache_name, input_class) pairs (graph, file-bytes, model-artifact-bytes/version, preamble-module, categorical-levels); for each, mutate just that input and assert the relevant key changes -- a single registry of output-affecting inputs that every new cache must extend. This is the architecture's named 'fingerprint-COMPLETENESS dossier' as an executable gate.
findings.prevents: Clusters C3 (model-artifact/preamble/id-keyed), C11 (mtime ms-bucket), C12 (duplicate-key divergence), plus V034 (NaN-set non-determinism) and V035 (non-injective node/extra-key join). Stale-served-as-fresh across preview/trace/deploy.

findings.title: Deploy validate-vs-serve has no byte-identical-artifact assertion; the test-before-live gate can load a different model than the container serves
findings.location: src/haute/deploy/_validators.py (score_test_quotes without artifact_paths); src/haute/deploy/_schema.py (infer_output_schema without bundled artifacts); src/haute/deploy/_scorer.py:605-704 (V044 modelScore passthrough when nothing bundled)
findings.description: Cluster C4 (and V044) is the only class that can mis-price a LIVE served quote: the 'test before live' gate scores test quotes and infers output schema WITHOUT passing bundled artifact_paths, so validation loads a model live from MLflow (version='latest', mutable) that can differ from the container's bundled artifact, and skips the contract check. V044 compounds it: a modelScore node with neither model nor contract bundled falls through to a silent passthrough at deploy time, bypassing the 'no model artifact' fail-loud guard. resolved.artifacts is already available at both call sites; nothing asserts validate and serve load the same bytes.
findings.recommended_guard: Add a deploy parity test: thread resolved.artifacts into both score_test_quotes and infer_output_schema, then assert (a) the artifact bytes/hash loaded at validate time equal the bytes bundled into the container, and (b) a modelScore node with no bundled artifact raises at deploy/validate time rather than serving passthrough (pins V044). A single 'validate and serve resolve byte-identical artifacts for every model node' assertion dissolves the class.
findings.prevents: Cluster C4 (validate-vs-serve divergence) and V044 (modelScore silent passthrough at deploy).

findings.title: Cross-language CI lanes never meet, and there is no contract-snapshot artifact shared between backend and frontend
findings.location: .github/workflows/ci.yml:13-159 (backend, frontend, browser-e2e are independent jobs); scripts/preflight.sh:131-238 (RUN_BACKEND and RUN_FRONTEND disjoint)
findings.description: Backend and frontend correctness are validated in separate CI jobs and separate preflight branches. The only place they meet is browser-e2e (Playwright), which exercises rendered behaviour, not contract shape. Every wire-contract obligation the architecture names (api/types.ts <-> types/guards.ts, NodeType list, default-config shapes, cache-identity tokens like structuralVersion) is therefore validated only by hand-kept mirrors on each side. There is no generated contract snapshot that both sides assert against, so any of clusters C16/C17 (source-blind caches, under-keyed preview slots, WS sync identity) plus the frontend NodeType drift (separate finding) can land without a unit-level red.
findings.recommended_guard: Introduce a generated contract-snapshot step: backend emits a single contracts.json (NodeType values + per-type default config keys + wire field names + the cache-identity token contract) consumed by a frontend vitest that asserts the hand-written mirrors match. Add a dedicated 'contract-parity' CI job (or fold into both preflight lanes) so a contract change must update both sides in one PR. This makes the wire contract a tested artifact rather than a convention.
findings.prevents: Frontend/backend contract drift broadly; provides the harness home for the NodeType-parity guard and the structuralVersion/cache-identity agreement the architecture flags between client and backend.

results.note: The single most valuable prevention investment is an enforced module-level-singleton isolation registry (Finding 1). The conftest's 11 hand-written autouse reset fixtures (_trace/_preview cache, default_bus, admission reservations, pipeline_dir lru_cache, dual-cache session, project_root, job stores) are not a design solution -- they are 11 separate scars, each added reactively AFTER a state-leak regression bit someone. Meanwhile ~17 OTHER mutable module-level singletons in src/haute/ (_feature_validation_cache, _contract_cache, _model_cache, _local_model_cache, _runtime_path_fingerprint_memo, _pipeline_index, _module_deps, _sandbox._validation_cache, _last_broadcast_fp, _self_write_paths, ...) have NO autouse isolation -- they are reset only inside the one test file that happens to exercise them, so a leak from any other test is silent. This IS the dominant bug class in the audit catalog (stale-cache/state-bleed findings 14, 15, 34, 36, 40, 54, 60). A registry meta-test that fails when a new module-level mutable global appears without a declared reset hook (or explicit exemption) -- mirroring the proven test_test_debt.py fingerprint-ratchet pattern already in the repo -- converts the reactive conftest treadmill into a forcing function, dissolving the whole class at the prevention layer and making the globals injectable/documented rather than ad-hoc. That is strictly higher leverage than any individual coverage/threshold tweak.

findings.title: No guardrail forces new module-level mutable singletons to be test-isolated; conftest resets are reactive scars covering <40% of them
findings.location: tests/conftest.py:20-188 (11 autouse reset fixtures) vs. ~28 module-level mutable globals across src/haute/ (e.g. _model_scorer.py:77 _feature_validation_cache, _model_scorer.py:80 _feature_validation_last_entry, modelling/_feature_contract.py:266 _contract_cache, _mlflow_io.py:207 _model_cache, deploy/_scorer.py:81 _local_model_cache, execution.py:328 _runtime_path_fingerprint_memo, routes/_helpers.py:493 _pipeline_index, routes/_helpers.py:576 _module_deps, routes/_helpers.py:251 _self_write_paths, _sandbox.py:273 _validation_cache, server.py:493 _last_broadcast_fp)
findings.description: The conftest contains 11 hand-maintained autouse fixtures, each clearing one process-wide singleton, and every docstring admits it was added AFTER a specific leak (e.g. _clear_pipeline_dir_cache: 'without this, save tests delete real config files'; _clear_dual_cache_session: 'would let one test's working-layer state spill into another's emitter precedence check'). This is the reactive-patch anti-pattern: a leak is found in production-of-tests, a bespoke reset is bolted on, repeat. Crucially, a grep of src/haute shows ~28 mutable module-level globals (dicts/sets/caches/counters), but only ~11 are reset in conftest. The unguarded remainder (_feature_validation_cache, _contract_cache, _model_cache, _local_model_cache, _runtime_path_fingerprint_memo, _pipeline_index, _module_deps, _sandbox._validation_cache, etc.) are reset ONLY inside the single test file that exercises them locally -- so a leak originating in any OTHER test is invisible and order-dependent. This same state-bleed/stale-cache mechanism is the largest cluster in the audit catalog: findings 14 (size+mtime cache serves stale), 15 (preamble fingerprint stale), 34 (stale per-port parquet judged fresh), 36 (preview LRU keyed by nodeId alone), 40 (ms-bucket cache coarseness), 54 (_validation_cache keyed on id()), 60 (unbounded _validation_cache). The next such global added with no fixture will leak silently and only surface as a flaky, order-dependent failure under -n4 xdist.
findings.recommended_guard: Add a registry meta-test (tests/test_module_singleton_isolation.py) that AST-scans src/haute/ for module-level assignments whose value is a mutable container or known cache type (dict/set/list literals, Counter, WeakValueDictionary, FingerprintCache, LRUCache, StatGatedCache, lru_cache-decorated funcs, ContextVar) and asserts each is in one of two reviewed sets: (a) HAS_TEST_RESET -- a global with an exported _clear_*_for_tests/cache_clear/invalidate hook that conftest invokes autouse, or (b) EXEMPT -- documented immutable-after-import or per-request-scoped, with a one-line rationale. New globals fail CI until classified. Reuse the exact fingerprint-ratchet design already proven in tests/test_test_debt.py (path+scope+normalized-source SHA, _EXPECTED set, stale-by date). Pair it with a single conftest fixture that iterates a central RESETTABLE_SINGLETONS list calling each hook, replacing the 11 bespoke fixtures with one data-driven loop.
findings.prevents: The entire stale-cache / cross-test state-bleed class: catalog findings 14, 15, 34, 36, 40, 54, 60, plus every future module-global leak. Also prevents the recurring maintenance cost the 11 existing fixtures document.

findings.title: filterwarnings escalates only RuntimeWarning to error; Deprecation/Future/Resource/Pending warnings are swallowed, so silent dependency-drift and unclosed-resource bugs never fail CI
findings.location: pyproject.toml:148-152 (filterwarnings = ['error::RuntimeWarning', 'ignore:Mean of empty slice...', 'ignore:invalid value encountered in scalar divide...'])
findings.description: The warnings-as-errors policy is scoped to RuntimeWarning ONLY. DeprecationWarning, FutureWarning (which polars and pydantic emit aggressively across version bumps), ResourceWarning (unclosed files/sockets -- directly relevant given the catalog's leak findings 52 'cancelled fit leaks worker thread/Pool/train_dir' and 61 'PermissionError on Windows when a concurrent reader has the parquet open'), and PendingDeprecationWarning all pass silently. The project pins polars>=1.39,<2 and pydantic>=2.12,<3 with wide ranges; a minor bump that deprecates an API used on the pricing path produces a FutureWarning that no test will ever fail on, so the divergence ships. The two ignore-entries are unanchored substring filters (no module qualifier), so 'ignore:invalid value encountered in scalar divide' silences that RuntimeWarning from ANY library, not just the intended numeric kernel -- broader than necessary and could mask a genuine divide-by-zero in pricing math. There is no test asserting the filterwarnings policy itself (e.g. that the error:: escalation is present and the ignores are anchored).
findings.recommended_guard: Escalate to 'error' as the default and downgrade specific, module-anchored exceptions: filterwarnings = ['error', 'ignore::DeprecationWarning:<third_party_module>', ...] with each ignore carrying a message+module qualifier and a comment naming the upstream issue. At minimum add 'error::DeprecationWarning:haute', 'error::FutureWarning', 'error::ResourceWarning' so first-party deprecations and unclosed resources fail. Anchor the two existing numeric ignores to their emitting module. Add a config meta-test asserting the policy contains an 'error' escalation for these categories (so a future PR can't quietly relax it), analogous to test_check_critical_coverage's gate-config validation.
findings.prevents: Silent polars/pydantic API drift on the pricing path (the 'two implementations diverge' class -- catalog 11/23/29/47/50), and unclosed-resource leaks (catalog 52, 61). Turns dependency upgrades into loud, fixable CI failures.

findings.title: A perf-named test that is not marked `perf` is collected by NEITHER lane and silently never runs
findings.location: scripts/run_perf_suite.py:226-241 (_build_pytest_args hardcodes '-m perf'); pyproject.toml:142 (addopts = "-m 'not perf'"); tests/test_scoring_prep_perf.py:536 and tests/test_cache_perf_fixes.py:709 mark only ONE function each, top-level files outside tests/performance/
findings.description: Perf coverage is partitioned by a single marker with no structural backstop. The default suite runs `-m 'not perf'` and the perf lane runs `-m perf`. A test that is perf-shaped (slow, benchmark-style) but where the author forgot @pytest.mark.perf -- or added a second perf function to test_scoring_prep_perf.py / test_cache_perf_fixes.py without remarking it (those files mark exactly one function each, not a module-level pytestmark like the tests/performance/ files use) -- is excluded from the perf lane AND, if it is slow, drags the default suite or gets caught by the 60s default timeout. Conversely the perf lane's _budget_violations correctly fails on zero-collected and on skips/xfails, but it cannot detect a perf test that was never marked, because collection never sees it. There is no guard that 'every test under tests/performance/ carries the perf marker' or 'every *_perf.py test function is marked perf', so the perf lane's breadth silently erodes -- the lane proves only that the marked subset is fast, never that the perf-relevant surface is the marked subset.
findings.recommended_guard: Add a structural test (extend test_performance_docs.py or a new test) that AST-scans tests/performance/**/*.py and tests/**/*_perf.py and asserts every test function/class is covered by the perf marker (module pytestmark or decorator). Optionally enforce the inverse: any test whose default-suite call-phase duration exceeds a threshold (already measured via --durations) must be either marked perf or marked slow -- a ratchet on the slowest-N. Standardise the two top-level perf files onto a module-level `pytestmark = pytest.mark.perf` to match tests/performance/.
findings.prevents: Silent perf-coverage erosion (a perf regression in an unmarked test is invisible) and accidental slow tests in the default lane. Complements the existing zero-collected guard which only fires when the WHOLE lane is empty.

findings.title: Mutation-target set covers 3 of ~18 critical-coverage modules; the highest-risk silent-divergence files have no mutation gate
findings.location: mutation/targets.json:3-22 (job-store, path-resolution, registry) vs pyproject.toml:170-287 (18 critical_coverage files); tests/test_mutation_suite_runner.py:28-47 pins exactly those 3
findings.description: Mutation testing -- the only gate that proves tests actually ASSERT behaviour rather than merely execute lines -- runs against just 3 modules. The critical_coverage config itself declares 18 files 'high-risk', and the audit catalog's worst findings live in modules with NO mutation target: executor.py (finding 19 duplicate-node-id collapse, 30 enforce_project_root=False arbitrary read), parser.py / _parser_regex.py / _parser_submodels.py (6 regex fallback drops submodels, 20 async nodes dropped, 21/22 submodel edge/overwrite loss), _model_scorer.py (24 predict_proba vs hard label, 54 id()-keyed cache), _json_shred.py (4 silent row inflation, 34 stale parquet judged fresh), _ram_estimate.py (31 ignores cgroup limits). These are precisely 'a mutated branch survives because no test asserts the consequence' bugs -- the class mutation testing exists to catch -- yet they are unmonitored. The test_mutation_suite_runner.py test hard-codes the 3-target set as correct, so the gap is frozen as intended rather than flagged as debt. The runner infrastructure (per-target thresholds, PR-smoke selection, manifest) is excellent; it is simply pointed at too little.
findings.recommended_guard: Add a coverage-parity meta-test: assert every file in [tool.haute.critical_coverage.files] either has a mutation target in mutation/targets.json OR appears in an explicit, dated MUTATION_BACKLOG exemption set with a rationale (same ratchet shape as test_test_debt). This makes the 15 uncovered critical modules visible, reviewed debt with a burn-down, instead of an invisible gap. Prioritise adding targets for executor.py, parser.py, and _model_scorer.py (the modules whose survivors map to the catalog's high-severity silent-divergence findings). Keep the bounded PR-smoke selection so wall-clock stays manageable.
findings.prevents: Silent-divergence / dropped-input bugs where lines are covered but no assertion exists (catalog 4, 6, 19, 20, 21, 22, 24, 30, 34) -- the exact class line-coverage cannot detect and mutation can.

findings.title: Critical-coverage ratchet has no anti-regression floor: thresholds can be silently lowered, and two files already encode a TODO/temporary loosening with no enforced burn-back
findings.location: scripts/check_critical_coverage.py (compares actual>=threshold but never compares threshold against a committed baseline); pyproject.toml:271-280 (optimiser.py rationale: 'TODO: ratchet back to 97/95'), pyproject.toml:259-262 (json_cache.py: 'restored to 90% (was temporarily lowered to 87%)')
findings.description: The gate enforces actual-coverage >= declared-threshold, but nothing enforces declared-threshold >= previously-declared-threshold. A PR that drops a file's min_branch_coverage from 95 to 80 to make a red build green passes every check (the gate, the meta-test test_check_critical_coverage, and preflight) with no signal that protection was weakened. The config already contains evidence this happens organically: optimiser.py was recalibrated down ('Recalibrated when the module grew ~4x') with a TODO to ratchet back that nothing enforces, and json_cache.py's comment records a prior temporary lowering to 87%. The user's own MEMORY explicitly flags 'No coverage gaming -- never lower the gate', yet the tooling permits exactly that. A ratchet whose only direction is documented-in-a-comment is not a ratchet. (Separately, threshold loosening is the gateway to the under-asserted-code class the mutation gap above also addresses.)
findings.recommended_guard: Add a baseline-comparison test: store the current per-file thresholds as a committed snapshot (or read them from git HEAD/main) and fail if any min_statement_coverage or min_branch_coverage in pyproject.toml decreases relative to baseline without an explicit, dated, reviewed exemption entry. Encode any intentional temporary loosening (optimiser.py 97->95) as a dated debt entry with a burn-back deadline (mirror _DEBT_REVIEW_BY in test_test_debt) so a stale loosening fails CI after the date. This makes the ratchet monotonic-by-construction and turns the existing TODO comments into enforced obligations.
findings.prevents: Coverage-gaming via threshold relaxation (directly enforces the user's documented 'never lower the gate' rule) and the slow erosion of the under-asserted-code surface that feeds the silent-bug class.

findings.title: Process-wide singleton isolation is undefended against test-order and xdist sharding flakiness; no randomized-order or isolation-failure detection exists
findings.location: tests/conftest.py:20-188 (all isolation is autouse per-test reset within a worker); scripts/run_perf_suite.py / preflight.sh:165 (pytest -n "$PYTEST_WORKERS" with default ordering, no -p randomly)
findings.description: Every isolation fixture clears state per-test, which only protects against leakage when the NEXT test runs in the same worker. The suite runs under xdist (-n4) which sharded by file, so the de-facto execution order is stable-but-arbitrary and differs from a serial run. Two failure modes are undetected: (1) a singleton with no reset fixture (see Finding 1) leaks within a worker and produces an order-dependent pass/fail that is reproducible only under one specific shard assignment -- invisible until an unrelated PR reshuffles files across workers; (2) a fixture that clears BEFORE but not AFTER (or vice-versa) leaves a window. The catalog's flaky-by-shared-state findings (54 id()-keyed cache collision, 60 unbounded accumulation, 40 ms-bucket collision) are exactly the shape that randomized ordering surfaces. There is no scheduled job that runs the suite with -p randomly (random seed) or with --forked, so cross-test contamination has no detector; it is found only when it breaks main.
findings.recommended_guard: Add a scheduled (weekly, like mutation/perf) CI leg that runs the full backend suite with pytest-randomly (random order, logged seed) AND a second pass with -p no:cacheprovider + a fresh worker-per-test or --forked sampling on the highest-risk modules. A failure means a real isolation bug; the logged seed makes it reproducible. This is the dynamic complement to Finding 1's static registry: the registry prevents un-isolated globals; the randomized run catches isolation logic that is present but wrong (clear-before-only, missing teardown).
findings.prevents: Order-dependent flakiness from shared-state contamination (catalog 40, 54, 60) and broken-but-present isolation fixtures; surfaces leaks before they hit main rather than after a file-shuffle exposes them.

findings.title: conftest globally monkeypatches StarletteTestClient.__init__ and httpx.AsyncClient.__init__ for every test, a broad autouse mutation of third-party class internals with no scoping or contract test
findings.location: tests/conftest.py:35-75 (_local_session_auth_for_route_clients autouse, monkeypatch.setattr on StarletteTestClient.__init__ and httpx.AsyncClient.__init__)
findings.description: An autouse fixture rewrites the constructors of two third-party HTTP-client classes for the entire suite to inject a session token and rewrite base_url from testserver->localhost. This is a global behavioural override of library internals applied to tests that may have nothing to do with route auth. Risks: (1) it silently changes base_url for any AsyncClient using ASGITransport at testserver, which can mask a test that intended to assert default-URL behaviour; (2) it couples every test to Starlette/httpx private __init__ signatures -- an httpx minor bump that changes __init__ kwargs breaks the whole suite at once with an opaque error, not just auth tests; (3) being autouse, it grants ambient authentication, so a test cannot easily verify the UNauthenticated 401 path without extra effort, weakening coverage of the security boundary (related to catalog 30's auth-boundary concerns). It is the kind of 'convenience global' the codebase's own anti-fallback principle warns against.
findings.recommended_guard: Convert to an explicit, named fixture (e.g. authed_client) that route tests opt into, leaving a separate fixture for unauthenticated probes -- making auth an explicit dimension of each test rather than ambient. If a global default must remain, add a contract test that constructs a bare httpx.AsyncClient/TestClient and asserts the patched signature still accepts the expected kwargs, so an httpx/starlette bump fails with a clear, localized message instead of cascading across the suite.
findings.prevents: Suite-wide opaque breakage on httpx/starlette upgrades, and under-tested unauthenticated/401 security paths (supports catalog 30). Reduces hidden coupling to library internals.
